source_routes.name: Canonical slot state and exact-output acceptance

facts.detail: Social tariffs are lower-cost packages for customers claiming Universal Credit, Pension Credit and certain other benefits.
A household member claiming Universal Credit can support eligibility for available tariffs.
Major providers also include Pension Credit, Employment and Support Allowance, Jobseeker's Allowance and Income Support.
The benefit recipient needs to be the main person named on the contract.

guard_streams.write_limit: Benefit eligibility does not prove that a tariff or network is available at a specific parcel.

facts.detail: The Ofcom list states current social-tariff prices range from £10 to £24.
Most listed broadband social tariffs offer speeds above 30 Mbit/s.
Setup should cost nothing or only a small amount disclosed before sign-up.
Social tariffs are delivered like normal packages but at a lower price.

guard_streams.write_limit: Advertised tariff price and speed are retail-package facts, not parcel-level measured performance.

facts.detail: Where the current provider offers a social tariff, an eligible customer can switch to it at any time without charge.
The social-tariff price should not rise during the contract.
Customers should not pay a fee to leave a social tariff before contract end.
Ofcom explicitly notes providers may not cover every premise in a listed region and directs users to coverage checks.

guard_streams.write_limit: Switching and exit protections cannot establish exact address serviceability.

facts.detail: New contracts since January 2025 cannot use inflation-linked or percentage-based price-rise terms.
Any specified increase must be set out clearly in pounds and pence before sign-up.
Price-rise information must be displayed prominently and transparently.
Providers must also state when monthly-price changes will occur.

guard_streams.write_limit: Price transparency is a consumer-contract duty and not network evidence.

facts.detail: Contracts signed before 17 January 2025 may still contain inflation-linked or percentage terms.
An increase not specified in the contract, or above the stated increase, requires at least 30 days notice.
The customer must then receive 30 days to exit without an exit fee.
Eligible customers should be able to move to their provider's social tariff without a penalty even while in contract.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract exit rights do not identify broadband availability at a premise.

facts.detail: Ofcom research found only 16% of affected broadband customers were aware of and could identify the inflation-linked rise.
The equivalent figure for affected pay-monthly mobile customers was 12%.
Ofcom reported 55% of broadband customers did not know what CPI and RPI measure.
The corresponding share for pay-monthly mobile customers was 58%.

guard_streams.write_limit: Consumer-understanding research is aggregate evidence, not exact network coverage.

facts.detail: New telecoms service contracts are typically 12, 18 or 24 months.
Providers must tell customers when the contract is ending and how much a new deal could save.
Out-of-contract customers are advised to compare offers and ask the current provider to match or beat them.
Bundles can be cheaper for customers needing multiple services but may be less flexible.

guard_streams.write_limit: Money-saving guidance and contract status cannot populate parcel coverage fields.

facts.detail: Ofcom measured mobile performance across 24 key railway-line segments in England, Scotland and Wales.
Good performance required at least 5 Mbit/s download.
Good performance required at least 1.5 Mbit/s upload.
Good performance also required response time of 50 milliseconds or less.

guard_streams.write_limit: Rail-route measurements do not establish stationary parcel coverage.

facts.detail: EE met the defined good-performance standard on 42% of measured railway segments.
Three met the standard on 21% of measured segments.
O2 met the standard on 20% and Vodafone on 17% of measured segments.
Train-company onboard Wi-Fi performed well only 1% of the time in the study.

guard_streams.write_limit: Operator and onboard-Wi-Fi rail results cannot be promoted to parcel rows.

facts.detail: Ofcom's discussion paper defines desired good mobile connectivity and explores how to improve it.
Ofcom states current UK mobile connectivity is too often not good enough.
Improvement requires coordinated action from industry, government, local authorities, landlords and others.
Ofcom plans an early-2027 update on lessons, priorities and next steps.

guard_streams.write_limit: A discussion paper and future priorities are not parcel-level measurements.

guard_streams.source: BDUK June and July 2026 contract progress

facts.detail: Call-off 5 built count rose from 880 in June to 2,260 in July while contracted scope remained 35,300.
Call-off 7 changed from 22,600 contracted and 170 built in June to 22,980 contracted and 1,010 built in July.
The monthly total changed from 839,340 contracted and 271,460 built in June to 838,490 contracted and 287,510 built in July.
Both releases state the data covers initial scope, is rounded and lagged, and must not be used to assess contractual milestones.

guard_streams.write_limit: Month-to-month management movement is not exact parcel-delivery evidence.
